title: Derived extension-by-zero base change
statement:
Let $\square$ be an
open-immersion square and let
$\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. For every
$K\in D^+(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$ the map of
[lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] is an isomorphism

$$
g^{-1}j_!K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!g_U^{-1}K
$$

in $D^+(X'_{\Et},\Lambda)$, and the isomorphism is natural in $K$,
is the identity for $g=\operatorname{id}$, and is compatible with
pasting of open-immersion squares.

proof.text: Work throughout with sheaves of modules over the constant finite ring $\Lambda$ on the small etale sites. The square gives open immersions $j,j'$ and arbitrary scheme morphisms $g,g_U$. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] the two inverse images are additive and exact on these module categories, and by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] the two extensions by zero are additive and exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to each of the four functors: their termwise complex functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms and induce functors on $D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], $H^r(F_DK)\cong F(H^rK)$, so each preserves the lower cohomological bound of $K$ and restricts to $D^+$. Thus the two composite functors in the statement have exactly the stated source and target; no resolution or flatness assumption on a scheme morphism is required.

Write $b_{g,F}:g^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!g_U^{-1}F$ for the module-sheaf isomorphism of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change]. To remove the ambiguity of the truncated sentence in that imported statement, use the precise module-sheaf construction [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map] and its isomorphism theorem [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], specialized to the present open immersions: $b$ is the inverse of their $\beta$. Make its canonical normalization explicit. Let $\eta_j:F\to j^{-1}j_!F$ be the unit. The unit is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-unit-iso] on underlying abelian sheaves; it is module-linear by the module adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction], so its inverse is also module-linear (apply the inverse to $\lambda\eta_j(s)=\eta_j(\lambda s)$). The commuting-square identification $s_g:g_U^{-1}j^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}j'^{-1}g^{-1}$ is obtained from the inverse-image composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear]. Under $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ the inverse map $a_{g,F}=b_{g,F}^{-1}$ is the transpose of $s_g\circ g_U^{-1}(\eta_{j,F})$. Equivalently, $a_{g,F}=\varepsilon_{j',g^{-1}j_!F}\circ j'_!(s_g\circ g_U^{-1}\eta_{j,F})$. Here is the comparison with the cited definition of $\beta$. Put $B=g^{-1}j_!F$. Transposing $\beta_F$ first under $j'_!\dashv j'^{-1}$ and then under $g_U^{-1}\dashv g_{U*}$ gives $\Ex^0_{\mathrm{flip},B}\circ j^{-1}(\eta_{g,j_!F})\circ\eta_{j,F}$ by that definition. The section formula in [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] gives $\Ex^0_{\mathrm{flip},B}\circ j^{-1}(\eta_{g,j_!F})=g_{U*}(s_{g,j_!F})\circ\eta_{g_U,j^{-1}j_!F}$: both maps send a local section to its pullback on the same fibre product. Naturality of $\eta_{g_U}$ and the triangle identity for $g_U^{-1}\dashv g_{U*}$ therefore give the single transpose $s_g\circ g_U^{-1}(\eta_{j,F})$. Thus $a=\beta$, the counit constructs $a$, and the map displayed in the item is $a^{-1}$. Naturality of the adjunction bijection and of the unit and square identification gives $a_{g,F'}\circ j'_!g_U^{-1}(t)=g^{-1}j_!(t)\circ a_{g,F}$ for every module morphism $t:F\to F'$; inversion gives the naturality equation for $b$. With both restrictions identified with $g_U^{-1}F$ through the units and $s_g$, the transpose formula says $j'^{-1}(a_{g,F})=\mathrm{id}$, and hence also $j'^{-1}(b_{g,F})=\mathrm{id}$.

Prove the sheaf-level identity and pasting before passing to complexes. For $g=\mathrm{id}_X$, use the identity inverse-image identifications: both sides are $j_!F$, and the transpose of $a_{\mathrm{id},F}$ is $\eta_{j,F}$, which is also the transpose of $\mathrm{id}_{j_!F}$. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives $a_{\mathrm{id},F}=\mathrm{id}$ and thus $b_{\mathrm{id},F}=\mathrm{id}$. For a second base change $h:X''\to X'$ let $U''=X''\times_{X'}U'$, with $j'':U''\hookrightarrow X''$ and $h_U:U''\to U'$. The composite to compare with $b_{g\circ h,F}$ is
$$h^{-1}g^{-1}j_!F\xrightarrow{h^{-1}b_{g,F}}h^{-1}j'_!g_U^{-1}F\xrightarrow{b_{h,g_U^{-1}F}}j''_!h_U^{-1}g_U^{-1}F.$$
Use [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear] to identify the endpoints with $(g\circ h)^{-1}j_!F$ and $j''_!(g_U\circ h_U)^{-1}F$. The composition and identity identifications are coherent on abelian sheaves by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition], hence on modules too: their maps are module-linear, and equality of underlying maps is equality of module maps. Restricting the displayed composite to $U''$ gives $\mathrm{id}\circ\mathrm{id}=\mathrm{id}$ by Step 2; restricting $b_{g\circ h,F}$ gives the same identity. To deduce equality without assuming stalk conservativity implies faithfulness, take inverses. Both inverse maps have source $j''_!(g_U\circ h_U)^{-1}F$. The adjunction bijection sends a map $v:j''_!A\to B$ to $j''^{-1}(v)\circ\eta_{j'',A}$. Their equal restrictions therefore give equal transposes, and injectivity gives equal inverse maps, hence equal maps. This proves pasting, including all endpoint composition identifications.
For clarity, the preceding comparison of inverse maps can be computed directly. Put $A=g_U^{-1}F$, $B=g^{-1}j_!F$ and $v=h^{-1}(a_{g,F})\circ a_{h,A}$. Its transpose under $j''_!\dashv j''^{-1}$ is
$$j''^{-1}(v)\circ\eta_{j'',h_U^{-1}A}
=j''^{-1}h^{-1}(a_{g,F})\circ s_{h,j'_!A}\circ h_U^{-1}\eta_{j',A}
=s_{h,B}\circ h_U^{-1}(j'^{-1}(a_{g,F})\circ\eta_{j',A})
=s_{h,B}\circ h_U^{-1}(s_{g,j_!F}\circ g_U^{-1}\eta_{j,F}).$$
The second equality is naturality of $s_h$, and the third is the transpose formula of Step 2. Associativity of the composition identifications identifies the last expression with $s_{g\circ h,j_!F}\circ(g_U\circ h_U)^{-1}\eta_{j,F}$, the transpose of $a_{g\circ h,F}$.
Also check pasting in the open-immersion direction. Let $k:V\hookrightarrow U$, $V'=X'\times_XV$, $k':V'\hookrightarrow U'$, and $g_V:V'\to V$. Write $c:j_!k_!\xrightarrow{\sim}(j\circ k)_!$ and $c':j'_!k'_!\xrightarrow{\sim}(j'\circ k')_!$ for [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. The required equation is
$$c'_{g_V^{-1}F}\circ j'_!(b_{g_U,F}^{k})\circ b_{g,k_!F}^{j}
=b_{g,F}^{j\circ k}\circ g^{-1}(c_F).$$
Here the superscript names the open immersion used in the exchange. Use the restriction models supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]: on an etale object $W\to V$, restriction twice gives $G(W\to V\to U\to X)$, exactly restriction along $j\circ k$. The canonical comparison $c$ is the unique unit-compatible comparison of these left adjoints, as given by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] and [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Its unit equation is
$$(j\circ k)^{-1}(c_F)\circ k^{-1}(\eta_{j,k_!F})\circ\eta_{k,F}=\eta_{j\circ k,F}.$$
All three units are invertible by Step 2, so, after identification with $F$ through these units, the restriction of $c_F$ is the identity; the same equation applies to $c'$. Restrict the displayed pasting equation to $V'$. The restrictions of both $b$ maps and of $b^{j\circ k}$ are identities by Step 2. For the middle map on the left, naturality of $\eta_{j'}$ identifies $k'^{-1}j'^{-1}j'_!(b^k)$ with $k'^{-1}(b^k)$, again the identity. For the rightmost comparison, $s_{g,j\circ k}$ identifies the restriction of $g^{-1}(c_F)$ with $g_V^{-1}((j\circ k)^{-1}c_F)$, the identity by the unit equation. Thus both restrictions agree. Their inverses have source $(j'\circ k')_!g_V^{-1}F$; the adjunction for $j'\circ k'$ sends these inverses to the same map, so they are equal by injectivity. Inverting proves the equation. The associativity and identity clauses of [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] ensure these endpoint comparisons agree under iterated pasting.

proof.text:
For a cochain complex $K^\bullet$, set $B_K^r=b_{g,K^r}$. Step 2 applied to $d^r:K^r\to K^{r+1}$ gives
$$j'_!g_U^{-1}(d^r)\circ B_K^r=B_K^{r+1}\circ g^{-1}j_!(d^r).$$
Thus $B_K$ is a chain map, and its degreewise inverse is a chain map by the same equality multiplied by the inverses. The two composites are the identity in every degree, so $B_K$ is an isomorphism of complexes, natural in chain maps. Compose this natural isomorphism with the localization functor on the target. Step 1 says both composite complex functors invert quasi-isomorphisms. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] now descends $B$ to a natural isomorphism of the induced functors on derived categories. Write $\varphi_{F,K}:F_D(QK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(C(F)K)$ for the factorization maps of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. For two composable exact functors $F,G$, the actual comparison for their induced composite at $QK$ is
$$\psi_{G,F,K}=\varphi_{G,C(F)K}\circ G_D(\varphi_{F,K}):G_DF_D(QK)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(C(G)C(F)K).$$
It is natural in $K$ by naturality of the two $\varphi$ maps. These are precisely the $\phi_1,\phi_2$ required by clause (2) of the localization node for the two composites in this square. Therefore its formula gives the descended exchange component $\psi_{j'_!,g_U^{-1},K}^{-1}\circ Q(B_K)\circ\psi_{g^{-1},j_!,K}$. For three functors, both parenthesizations of $\psi$ expand to $\varphi_{H,C(G)C(F)K}\circ H_D(\varphi_{G,C(F)K})\circ H_DG_D(\varphi_{F,K})$; hence their coherence follows from functoriality, and equality on all $QK$ is detected by clause (3) of the localization node. Restrict to the full subcategory $D^+$, which both sides preserve by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below]. At an object represented by $K^\bullet$ the component is the class of $B_K$ after these identifications. It is therefore exactly the derived map of the underived base-change map, and is an isomorphism for every $K\in D^+(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Apply Step 3 in every degree of a representing complex. For the identity square, every component of $B_K$ is the identity, so its localized component is the identity. For the two pasted squares, Step 3 gives $B_{g\circ h,K}=B_{h,g_U^{-1}K}\circ h^{-1}(B_{g,K})$, with the termwise composition identifications at the endpoints. Localization preserves compositions and identities, so this equality holds at every localized complex. The inverse-image comparison identifications also descend by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Clause (3) of that node makes the resulting equality an equality of natural transformations on $D$, since it holds on every $QK^\bullet$. Restriction to $D^+$ gives the required identity and pasting compatibilities; naturality for all derived morphisms is already part of the descended natural isomorphism in Step 4. For pasting along $k$ and $j$, apply $Q$ degreewise to the last equation of Step 3, including $c$ and $c'$. Clause (2) descends these comparisons as well as both exchanges; it preserves their composition. The $\psi$ formulas of Step 4 identify their endpoints, and clause (3) detects equality after these identifications. Thus the vertical pasting equation also holds on $D^+$, with its identity and iterated composition comparisons.
